hitl_conditions: Humans retained where tasks are physical or exceptional (loading/unloading, manual goods inspection, exception handling); routine order release and AGV re-routing become automatic. 5G human-machine interfaces and ergonomic design sustain real-time worker-system communication.
key_finding: A proof-of-concept warehouse digital twin couples Ridge-regularised polynomial regression on real packing data (RMSE 14.72 s vs 19.04 s linear, 89% cohesion) with a grid-adapted A* pathfinder, plus Node-RED/Traccar/RFID and 5G, to auto-release orders and re-route AGVs after layout changes.

quotes.text: This research presents a novel approach to integrate human-based operations with AMR to generate a real-time digital twin of automated warehouses.

For model development, we employed linear and second-degree polynomial regression techniques. Linear regression assumes a linear relationship, while polynomial regression accommodates non-linear patterns.
Conversely, the polynomial regression model exhibited superior performance by attaining a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) value of 14.72 seconds.

The present study introduces a significant alteration in the methodology employed, wherein a bespoke heuristic function is employed to direct the A* algorithm, which is specifically tailored to suit a warehouse layout that is based on a grid system.

quotes.text: Once the ETA of the vehicle aligns with the projected duration for processing the order, the order is authorised for immediate execution.

Notwithstanding the considerable degree of automation, human labourers play a crucial role in specific tasks, including the loading and unloading of cargo, the manual inspection of goods, and the management of exceptional scenarios.
